etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From French chicanerie (“trickery”), from chicaner, from Middle French chicaner, borrowed from Middle Low German schicken, from Old Saxon *skikkian, from Proto-West Germanic *skikkijan (“to order, arrange”).
Related to German schicken (“to send, ship”), Middle English skekken (“to send forth, issue”).
senses: (uncountable) Deception by the use of trickery, quibbling, or subterfuge.
(countable) An individual act of trickery or deception.
